LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `iamRoleStatements`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<StpIamRoleStatement>`

Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by `connectTo`.

Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for
accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: js-bundle
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `joinDefaultVpc`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Connects the function to your VPC so it can reach databases, Redis, and other VPC-only resources.

Set this to `true` when the function must reach VPC-only resources such as a database with
`accessibilityMode: 'vpc'`/`'scoping-workloads-in-vpc'`, a Redis cluster, or EFS.

**Tradeoff:** The function loses direct internet access. It can still reach S3 and DynamoDB
(Stacktape auto-creates VPC endpoints), but calls to external APIs (Stripe, OpenAI, etc.) will fail.
If you need both VPC access and internet, use a `web-service` or `worker-service` instead.

Required when using `volumeMounts` (EFS or S3 Files).

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  dbMigrator:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `layers`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Lambda Layer ARNs to attach (shared libraries, custom runtimes, etc.).

Layers are zip archives with additional code/data mounted into the function.
Provide the layer ARN (e.g., from AWS console or another stack). Max 5 layers per function.

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  monitoredFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/handler.ts
      layers:
        - arn:aws:lambda:eu-west-1:464622532012:layer:Datadog-Extension:62
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logging`

- Required: no
- Type: `LambdaFunctionLogging`

Logging configuration (retention, forwarding).

Logs (`stdout`/`stderr`) are auto-sent to CloudWatch. View with `stacktape logs` or in the Stacktape Console.

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiHandler:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      logging:
        retentionDays: 30
        logForwarding:
          type: datadog
          properties:
            apiKey: $Secret('datadog-api-key')
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `memory`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Memory in MB (128 - 10,240). Also determines CPU power.

Lambda scales CPU proportionally to memory: 1,769 MB = 1 vCPU, 3,538 MB = 2 vCPUs, etc.
If your function is slow, increasing memory gives it more CPU, which often makes it faster
and cheaper overall (less execution time).

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  pdfRenderer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/pdf.ts
      memory: 3538
      timeout: 120
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `provisionedConcurrency`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Eliminates cold starts by keeping function instances warm and ready.

When a function hasn't been called recently, the first request can take 1-5+ seconds ("cold start").
This setting pre-warms the specified number of instances so they respond instantly.

**When to use:** User-facing APIs, web/mobile backends, or any function where response time matters.
Skip this for background jobs, cron tasks, or data pipelines.

**Cost:** You pay for each provisioned instance even when idle. Also increases deploy time by ~2-5 minutes.

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  checkoutApi:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/checkout.ts
      memory: 1024
      provisionedConcurrency: 5
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: storeApi
            method: POST
            path: /checkout
  storeApi:
    type: http-api-gateway
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `releaseCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `ReleaseCommand | option-2`

Run a command once on each deploy, inside the VPC, before any workload gets the new code.

Use it for database migrations. A function's package holds only its bundled code, so Stacktape builds an image of
the whole project and runs the command in a one-off ECS task, with this function's environment variables and its
access to the resources in `connectTo`. The deploy waits for the task, prints its logs, and stops if the command
fails, so the running version keeps serving.

Set `runWhenChanged` to your migration folder. Without it, each code change builds the image and runs the command.
Building the image needs Docker on the machine that deploys.

The old code keeps running against the new schema until the deploy finishes, so migrations must stay compatible
with it. A retry runs the command again, so it must be idempotent. Neither a failed deploy nor `stacktape rollback`
reverses what the command changed.

Choices:
- `ReleaseCommand` (`ReleaseCommand`) — A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.. Properties: `command: string`, `runWhenChanged?: Array<string>`, `timeout?: number`, `container?: string`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '17'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
      releaseCommand:
        command: npx prisma migrate deploy
        runWhenChanged:
          - prisma/migrations
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `reservedConcurrency`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Cap the maximum number of concurrent instances for this function.

Reserves this many execution slots exclusively for this function — other functions can't use them,
and this function can't scale beyond it. **No additional cost.**

Common uses:

Prevent overwhelming a database with too many connections
Guarantee capacity for critical functions
Throttle expensive downstream API calls

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  legacyDbWriter:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/write.ts
      reservedConcurrency: 10
      connectTo:
        - legacyDb
  legacyDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
```

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `10`

Max execution time in seconds. Function is killed if it exceeds this.

Maximum: 900 seconds (15 minutes). For longer tasks, use a `batch-job` or `worker-service`.

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions | option-2`

Distributed tracing for this function.

When omitted, the function inherits the stack-wide `stackConfig.tracing` setting. Set `false` to
opt this function out, `true` to opt it in with the stack-wide sampling, or an object to opt it
in with its own settings. Stacktape attaches the OpenTelemetry instrumentation automatically —
no code changes required.

Choices:
- `TracingOptions` (`TracingOptions`). Properties: `enabled?: boolean`, `samplingRate?: number`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  noisyWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      tracing: false
```

LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `url`

- Required: no
- Type: `LambdaUrlConfig`

Give this function its own HTTPS URL (no API Gateway needed).

Simpler and cheaper than an API Gateway for single-function endpoints.
URL format: `https://{id}.lambda-url.{region}.on.aws`

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  webhookReceiver:
    type: function
    properties:

        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/webhook.ts

        enabled: true
        authMode: NONE
```

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `volumeMounts`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<efs | s3files>`

Persistent file-system mounts shared across invocations and functions.

Unlike `/tmp`, mounted file systems persist independently from the function runtime and can be
shared across multiple functions.
Requires `joinDefaultVpc: true` (Stacktape will remind you if you forget).

Choices:
- `efs` (`LambdaEfsMount`). Properties: `efsFilesystemName: string`, `rootDirectory?: string`, `mountPath: string`.
- `s3files` (`LambdaS3FilesMount`). Properties: `accessPointArn: option-1 | option-2`, `mountPath: string`.

docs.title: LambdaFunctionProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  sharedDataFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/handler.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      volumeMounts:
        - type: efs
          properties:
            efsFilesystemName: sharedStorage
            mountPath: /mnt/data
  sharedStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
```

A script that runs remotely on a bastion server.

BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `assumeRoleOfResource`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Assume Role of Resource

The name of a deployed resource whose IAM role the script should assume. This grants the script the same permissions as the specified resource.

The resource must be deployed before the script is executed. Stacktape injects temporary AWS credentials as environment variables, which are automatically used by most AWS SDKs and CLIs.

**Supported Resource Types:**

`function`
`batch-job`
`worker-service`
`web-service`
`private-service`
`multi-container-workload`
`nextjs-web`
`astro-web`
`nuxt-web`
`sveltekit-web`
`solidstart-web`
`tanstack-web`
`remix-web`

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  invokeAsApi:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeScript: scripts/admin-task.ts
      assumeRoleOfResource: api
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      connectTo:
        - dataBucket
  dataBucket:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Connect To

A list of resources the script needs to interact with. Stacktape automatically injects environment variables with connection details for each specified resource.

Environment variable names are in the format `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[VARIABLE_NAME]` (e.g., `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`).

**Injected Variables by Resource Type:**

**`Bucket`**: `NAME`, `ARN`
**`DynamoDbTable`**: `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`
**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`**: `CONNECTION_STRING`
**`RelationalDatabase`**: `CONNECTION_STRING`, `JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`. For Aurora clusters, `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_JDBC_CONNECTION_STRING`, and `READER_HOST` are also included.
**`Redis`**: `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`
**`EventBus`**: `ARN`
**`Function`**: `ARN`
**`BatchJob`**: `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`
**`UserAuthPool`**: `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`
**`SnsTopic`**: `ARN`, `NAME`
**`SqsQueue`**: `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`
**`UpstashKafkaTopic`**: `TOPIC_NAME`, `TOPIC_ID`, `USERNAME`, `PASSWORD`, `TCP_ENDPOINT`, `REST_URL`
**`UpstashRedis`**: `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`
**`PrivateService`**: `ADDRESS`
**`WebService`**: `URL`

## Property: `cwd`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `/`

Working Directory

The directory on the bastion host where the command will be executed.

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  runScript:
    type: bastion-script
    properties:
      bastionResource: jumpBox
      executeCommand: ./maintenance.sh
      cwd: /opt/scripts
resources:
  jumpBox:
    type: bastion
    properties:
      instanceSize: t3.micro
```

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment Variables

A list of environment variables to pass to the script or command.

Values can be:

A static string, number, or boolean.
The result of a [custom directive](https://docs.stacktape.com/configuration/directives/#custom-directives).
A reference to another resource's parameter using the [`$ResourceParam` directive](https://docs.stacktape.com/configuration/referenceable-parameters/).
A value from a [secret](https://docs.stacktape.com/configuration/secrets/) using the [`$Secret` directive](https://docs.stacktape.com/configuration/directives/#secret).

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  seed:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeScript: scripts/seed.ts
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
        - name: API_KEY
          value: $Secret('seed-api-key')
resources:
  table:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: id
          type: string
```

BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `executeCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Execute Command

A single terminal command to execute on the bastion host. Logs from the execution are streamed to your terminal.

You can use either `executeCommand` or `executeCommands`, but not both.

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  pingDb:
    type: bastion-script
    properties:
      bastionResource: jumpBox
      executeCommand: pg_isready -h $STP_PRIVATE_DB_HOST
      connectTo:
        - privateDb
resources:
  jumpBox:
    type: bastion
    properties:
      instanceSize: t3.micro
  privateDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
```

BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `executeCommands`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Execute Commands

A list of terminal commands to execute sequentially as a script on the bastion host. Logs from the execution are streamed to your terminal.

You can use either `executeCommand` or `executeCommands`, but not both.

docs.title: BastionScriptProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  dbMaintenance:
    type: bastion-script

      bastionResource: jumpBox

        - psql -h $STP_PRIVATE_DB_HOST -c 'REINDEX DATABASE postgres;'

        - privateDb

    properties:
      instanceSize: t3.micro
  privateDb:

    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc

        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content: # DeploymentConfig API Reference

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `autoRollback`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Roll a failed deployment back automatically instead of keeping what it created.

By default, a failed deployment keeps every resource it created or updated, and the next
deployment continues from the failure. An update that replaces existing resources still rolls
back, because CloudFormation can only replace resources in a deployment it may roll back. A failed first deployment keeps, for example, a database
that took minutes to create; a failed update keeps the resources that updated. Fix the error and
deploy again. To undo a failed update instead, run `stacktape stack recover`; to remove a failed
first deployment, run `stacktape delete`.

With `autoRollback: true`, a failed update rolls back to the last successful deployment and a
failed first deployment deletes the stack. It is on by default when `triggerRollbackOnAlarms` or
`monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes` is set, and cannot be turned off then.
The `--auto-rollback` flag of `stacktape deploy` overrides it for one deployment.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  autoRollback: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `cloudformationRoleArn`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

IAM role for CloudFormation to assume during create/update/delete operations.

Use this when your deploy user has limited permissions and CloudFormation needs
a more privileged role to manage resources. The role is persisted across deployments
and reused for delete/rollback even if removed from config later.

The deploy user itself still creates and deletes the stack's deployment bucket
(`stp-deployment-bucket-*`) and ECR repository (`*-stp-multi-container-workload-repo`):
it needs `s3:CreateBucket`, `s3:PutBucketPolicy`, `s3:PutBucketCORS`,
`s3:PutAccelerateConfiguration`, `s3:PutBucketTagging`, `s3:DeleteBucket`,
`ecr:CreateRepository`, `ecr:PutLifecyclePolicy`, `ecr:TagResource` and
`ecr:DeleteRepository` on them, besides reading and writing their contents.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  cloudformationRoleArn: arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/CloudFormationDeployRole
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `disableS3TransferAcceleration`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Disable faster uploads via S3 Transfer Acceleration.

Transfer Acceleration routes uploads through the nearest AWS edge location
for faster deploys, especially from distant regions. Adds a small cost per GB.
Automatically disabled in regions where it's not available.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  disableS3TransferAcceleration: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `errorTracking`

- Required: no
- Type: `ErrorTrackingConfig`

Error tracking: runtime errors read from this stack's logs and grouped in the Console.

On by default for every stage. Turn it off here, or limit it to some stages. See `ErrorTrackingConfig` for what is sent
and how sensitive text is masked.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  errorTracking:
    enabled: false
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `0`

How long (in minutes) to monitor rollback alarms after deployment completes.

If an alarm fires during this window, the stack rolls back automatically.
Only useful when `triggerRollbackOnAlarms` is configured. A monitoring period turns on `autoRollback`.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  triggerRollbackOnAlarms:
    - arn:aws:cloudwatch:eu-west-1:123456789012:alarm:high-error-rate
  monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes: 15
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `previousVersionsToKeep`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `10`

How many old deployment artifacts (Lambda bundles, container images) to keep.

Older versions are cleaned up automatically. Lower values save storage costs,
higher values make it easier to roll back to previous versions.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  previousVersionsToKeep: 3
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `publishEventsToArn`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

SNS topic ARNs to receive CloudFormation stack events during deployment.

Useful for monitoring deployments in external systems (Slack, PagerDuty, etc.).

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  publishEventsToArn:
    - arn:aws:sns:eu-west-1:123456789012:deployment-events
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `securityScanning`

- Required: no
- Type: `SecurityScanningConfig`

Security scanning of this stack's configuration on every deployment.

Enabled by default for every stage. The findings appear in the deploy output and in the Security section of
the Stacktape Console, where they can be reviewed, ignored or turned into organization-wide guardrails. Turn
scanning off for a stack, or limit it to selected stages, when a stack must not report anything. An
organization administrator can also choose per AWS account, in the Console's security settings, to skip the
dependency checks or turn scanning off; that choice applies to every stack deployed into the account.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  securityScanning:
    stages: [production]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `terminationProtection`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Prevents accidental stack deletion. Must be disabled before you can delete.

Recommended for production stacks. To delete a protected stack, first deploy with
`terminationProtection: false`, then run the delete command.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  terminationProtection: true
resources:
  prodDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      deletionProtection: true
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.r6g.large
```

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `triggerRollbackOnAlarms`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Alarms that trigger automatic rollback if they fire during deployment.

Specify alarm names (from `alarms` section) or ARNs. The alarm must already exist -
a newly created alarm only takes effect on the *next* deployment.

Use with `monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes` to keep watching after deploy completes.
Setting rollback alarms turns on `autoRollback`.

docs.title: DeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  triggerRollbackOnAlarms:
    - arn:aws:cloudwatch:eu-west-1:123456789012:alarm:high-error-rate
  monitoringTimeAfterDeploymentInMinutes: 10
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

# DevModeConfig API Reference

Dev Mode Configuration

docs.title: DevModeConfig API Reference
DevModeConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `remote`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Use the deployed AWS resource instead of a local emulation.

By default, databases, Redis, and DynamoDB run locally in Docker during dev mode.
Set to `true` to connect to the real deployed resource instead (must be deployed first).

Useful when local emulation doesn't match production behavior closely enough,
or when you need to work with real data.

docs.title: DevModeConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  myApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      connectTo:
        - sessionsTable
  sessionsTable:
    type: dynamo-db-table
    properties:
      primaryKey:
        partitionKey:
          name: id
          type: string
      dev:
        remote: true
```

DirectiveDefinition API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `filePath`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

File Path

The path to the file where the directive is defined, in the format `{file-path}:{handler}`.

If the `{handler}` is omitted:

For `.js` and `.ts` files, the `default` export is used.
For `.py` files, the `main` function is used.

docs.title: DirectiveDefinition API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
directives:
  - name: GetCommitSha
    filePath: directives/git.ts:getCommitSha
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      environment:
        - name: COMMIT_SHA
          value: $GetCommitSha()
```

DirectiveDefinition API Reference
docs.content:

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Directive Name

docs.content: # DomainConfiguration API Reference

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `domainName`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Your domain name (e.g., `mydomain.com` or `api.mydomain.com`).

Don't include the protocol (`https://`). The domain must have a Route53 hosted zone
in your AWS account, with your registrar's nameservers pointing to it.

Stacktape automatically creates a DNS record and provisions a free TLS certificate.

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        - domainName: api.example.com
```

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `customCertificateArn`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Use your own TLS certificate instead of the auto-generated one.

Provide the ARN of an ACM certificate from your AWS account.
Only needed if you have specific certificate requirements (e.g., EV/OV certs).
By default, Stacktape provisions and renews free certificates automatically.

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        - domainName: api.example.com
          customCertificateArn: arn:aws:acm:us-east-1:123456789012:certificate/abcd1234-ef56-7890-abcd-ef1234567890
```

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `disableDnsRecordCreation`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Skip DNS record creation for this domain.

Set to `true` if you manage DNS records yourself (e.g., through Cloudflare or another DNS provider).
Stacktape will still provision the TLS certificate but won't touch your DNS.

docs.title: DomainConfiguration API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  webApi:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      customDomains:
        - domainName: api.example.com
          disableDnsRecordCreation: true
```

EnvironmentVar API Reference

EnvironmentVar API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `value`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string | number | boolean`

Environment variable value. Numbers and booleans are converted to strings.

docs.title: ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference
docs.content: # ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference

docs.title: ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference
ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `enabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `true`

Records runtime errors from this stack's logs in the Stacktape Console.

When enabled, every deployment subscribes the stack's function and container log groups to Stacktape's error
detector. Matching error lines are grouped into issues (one per distinct error and resource) with their stack
traces and occurrence counts, shown on the Error tracking page and by `stacktape error list`.

What leaves your AWS account per error: the error message and type, the stack frames, the matching log line and
the request id. Known shapes of sensitive data (secrets and tokens, values under sensitive key names such as
`password` or `authorization`, email addresses, IP addresses, card numbers and user home paths) are masked before
the event is sent. Logs themselves stay in your account.

When disabled, no log subscriptions are created for this stack and nothing is sent. The Console also has an
organization-wide switch that turns error tracking off for every stack at once.

docs.title: ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stages`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Stages that record errors. When omitted or empty, every stage does.

Use it to keep short-lived preview stages out of the Error tracking page while production and staging report.

docs.title: ErrorTrackingConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  errorTracking:
    stages: [production, staging]
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

docs.title: Hooks API Reference
Hooks API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `afterBucketSync`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<NamedScriptLifecycleHook>`

Scripts to run after syncing bucket contents.

docs.title: Hooks API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  invalidateCache:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeCommand: node ./scripts/purge-cdn.js
hooks:
  afterBucketSync:
    - scriptName: invalidateCache
resources:
  assets:
    type: hosting-bucket

      uploadDirectoryPath: ./public
```

Hooks API Reference
docs.content:

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<NamedScriptLifecycleHook>`

Scripts to run after deleting the stack.

Only runs when `--config` and `--stage` are provided to the delete command.

```yaml
scripts:
```

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<NamedScriptLifecycleHook>`

Scripts to run after deploying. Common use: run database migrations, seed data.

```yaml
scripts:
```

Hooks API Reference

Hooks API Reference

docs.title: Hooks API Reference
Hooks API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `beforeDelete`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<NamedScriptLifecycleHook>`

Scripts to run before deleting the stack. Common use: export data, clean up external resources.

Only runs when `--config` and `--stage` are provided to the delete command.

docs.title: Hooks API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
scripts:
  exportData:
    type: local-script
    properties:
      executeCommand: node ./scripts/export-data.js
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
hooks:
  beforeDelete:
    - scriptName: exportData
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
```

## Property: `onFailure`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "continue" | "fail"`
- Default: `fail`

What happens when the script fails.

`fail`: the command stops and exits with an error, and the hooks listed after this one don't run. When an
`afterDeploy` hook fails, the deployment has already finished and stays live. The command still exits with an
error, so a CI job fails.
`continue`: the failure is printed as a warning and the command carries on.

Use `continue` for work that must not fail a deploy, such as sending a notification.

docs.content:
## Property: `type`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "ec2" | "gateway" | "ha-ec2"`

Which kind of NAT the stack runs.

**ec2**: one small EC2 instance (`t4g.nano` by default) managed by Stacktape. About $7/month, no per-GB
charge. If the instance dies, AWS replaces it, which takes about three minutes without outbound internet.
**ha-ec2**: one such instance per availability zone (two by default) with automatic failover. About $7/month
per zone. When an instance fails, Stacktape routes its zone through another zone's instance within about a
minute and routes back once the replacement is healthy; outbound calls from that zone fail during that minute
and open connections are reset.
**gateway**: AWS-managed NAT Gateways, one per availability zone. About $32/month per zone plus $0.045 per GB
processed. No instances, scales to 100 Gbps; the choice for high sustained throughput and strict uptime.

The shorthand `nat: ha-ec2` is the same as `nat: { type: ha-ec2 }`.

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat:
    type: ha-ec2
resources:
  worker:
    type: worker-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
NatSettings API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `availabilityZones`

- Required: no
- Type: `number: 2 | 3`
- Default: `2`

How many availability zones get their own NAT (`ha-ec2` and `gateway` only).

**2**: Balanced cost and availability.
**3**: Highest availability.

Each NAT gets a static Elastic IP that persists across deployments —
useful for IP whitelisting with external services.

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat:
    type: gateway
    availabilityZones: 3
resources:
  worker:
    type: worker-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
NatSettings API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `instanceSize`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `t4g.nano`

EC2 instance size of the NAT instances (`ec2` and `ha-ec2` only).

Must be an arm64 (Graviton) size, for example `t4g.nano`, `t4g.micro`, `t4g.small` or `c7gn.medium`.
`t4g.nano` bursts to 5 Gbps and is enough for most applications; pick a larger size for sustained
high throughput.

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat:
    type: ha-ec2
    instanceSize: t4g.small
resources:
  worker:
    type: worker-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

docs.title: NatSettings API Reference
ReleaseCommand API Reference
docs.content:
# ReleaseCommand API Reference

A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.

docs.title: ReleaseCommand API Reference
ReleaseCommand API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `command`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

The shell command to run, for example `npx prisma migrate deploy`.

It runs through `/bin/sh -c` in place of the image's entry point. If the image needs its entry point, call it in the
command. An image without a shell cannot run a release command.

docs.title: ReleaseCommand API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `container`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

The container to run the command in.

Required for a `multi-container-workload` with several containers. On other services, it runs in the main container.

docs.title: ReleaseCommand API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `runWhenChanged`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Run the command only when these files or directories changed.

Paths are relative to the project root and must exist. A deploy that changes none of them skips the command and can
stay on the fast path. Without this option, the command runs on each deploy that changes the image.

docs.title: ReleaseCommand API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `timeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `3300`

How long the command can run, in seconds. The deploy fails and the task stops when it runs longer.

docs.title: SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference
docs.content: # SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference

docs.title: SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference
SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `name`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Environment variable name exposed to the container (e.g., `DATABASE_PASSWORD`, `API_KEY`).

docs.title: SecretEnvironmentVar API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `valueFrom`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Secret source injected by the container runtime.

Use an exact `$SsmParam(...)` or `$Secret(...)` directive. Unlike `environment`, Stacktape passes only the
parameter or secret ARN to the container orchestrator; the sensitive value is never stored in the task
definition.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content: # SecurityScanningConfig API Reference

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `enabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `true`

Turns security scanning on or off for this stack.

When enabled, every deployment evaluates the resolved configuration against Stacktape's security rules, records
which packages the source tree and the rebuilt container images use (a CycloneDX inventory stored in the stack's
deployment bucket), and reports the findings and the inventory's location to the Security section of the
Stacktape Console, which grades the packages against known vulnerabilities. Findings describe risky settings,
for example a database reachable from the internet or a secret stored as a plain environment variable. When
disabled, nothing is evaluated, recorded or uploaded for this stack.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stages`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Limits security scanning to the listed stages.

When omitted or empty, every stage is scanned. Stage names are matched exactly.

docs.title: SecurityScanningConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
deploymentConfig:
  securityScanning:
    stages: [production, staging]
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content: # ServiceHelperContainer API Reference

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `containerType`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "always-running" | "run-on-init"`

When and how this sidecar container runs.

**`run-on-init`**: Must exit with code 0 before the main container starts. Use for migrations or setup.
**`always-running`**: Runs alongside the main container for its entire lifetime. If it crashes, the whole task fails.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      sideContainers:
        - name: migrations
          containerType: run-on-init
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `name`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Unique container name within this workload.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

How to build or specify the container image.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: dockerfile
            properties:
              buildContextPath: ./api
              dockerfilePath: Dockerfile
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dependsOn`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ContainerDependency>`

Start this container only after the listed containers reach a specific state.

E.g., wait for a database sidecar to be `HEALTHY` before starting the app container.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: migrations
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
          essential: false
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          dependsOn:
            - containerName: migrations
              condition: SUCCESS
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables injected at runtime. Use `$ResourceParam()` or `$Secret()` for dynamic values.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          environment:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: $ResourceParam('appDb', 'connectionString')
            - name: STRIPE_KEY
              value: $Secret('stripe', 'secretKey')
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - appDb
  appDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db', 'password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `essential`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`

If `true` (default), the entire workload restarts when this container fails.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
        - name: metrics-sidecar
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: prom/statsd-exporter:latest
          essential: false
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `internalHealthCheck`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerHealthCheck`

Command-based health check. If it fails on an essential container, the workload instance is replaced.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          internalHealthCheck:
            healthCheckCommand:
              - CMD-SHELL
              - curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
            intervalSeconds: 30
            retries: 3
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logging`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadContainerLogging`

Container logging (stdout/stderr). Sent to CloudWatch, viewable with `stacktape logs`.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          logging:
            retentionDays: 14
            disabled: false
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `secrets`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<SecretEnvironmentVar>`

Sensitive environment variables fetched by ECS instead of stored in the task definition.

Each `valueFrom` must be an exact `$SsmParam(...)` or `$Secret(...)` directive.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait after SIGTERM before SIGKILL (2-120).

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          stopTimeout: 60
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `volumeMounts`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ContainerEfsMount>`

Mount EFS volumes for persistent, shared storage across containers.

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          volumeMounts:
            - type: efs
              properties:
                efsFilesystemName: sharedStorage
                mountPath: /data
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
  sharedStorage:
    type: efs-filesystem
```

docs.title: ServiceHelperContainer API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content: # StackConfig API Reference

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `disableStackInfoSaving`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Stop saving stack info to a local file after each deployment.

By default, Stacktape saves resource details and custom outputs to
`.stacktape-stack-info/{stackName}.json` after every deploy.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  disableStackInfoSaving: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `nat`

- Required: no
- Type: `NatSettings | option-2`

NAT: outbound internet for workloads in the private subnets.

Who uses it:

container workloads with `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true` (they cannot run without it, so setting that flag
requires `nat`);
Lambda functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, which have no internet access at all until `nat` is set;
AgentCore runtimes that connect to VPC-only resources.

Pick `ec2` (one small instance, ~$7/month, no failover), `ha-ec2` (one instance per availability zone with
automatic failover, ~$7/month per zone) or `gateway` (AWS-managed NAT Gateways, ~$32/month per zone plus
$0.045 per GB). Switching between kinds keeps the VPC and subnets, but the public IPs change.

With `vpc.reuseVpc`, the reused VPC's own NAT is used and this setting creates nothing; set it to any kind to
place this stack's VPC functions in the reused VPC's private subnets.

Choices:
- `NatSettings` (`NatSettings`). Properties: `type: string: "ec2" | "gateway" | "ha-ec2"`, `instanceSize?: string`, `availabilityZones?: number: 2 | 3`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `outputs`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<StackOutput>`

Custom values to display and save after each deployment.

Use outputs to surface dynamic values like API URLs, database endpoints, or resource ARNs
that are only known after deployment. Outputs are:

Printed in the terminal after deploy
Saved to the stack info JSON file
Optionally exported for cross-stack references (via `export: true`)

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  outputs:
    - name: ApiUrl
      value: $ResourceParam('api', 'url')
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stackInfoDirectory`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `.stacktape-stack-info/`

Directory for the stack info JSON file.

Relative to the project root.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  stackInfoDirectory: ./build/stack-info
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stageType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "non-production" | "production"`

Explicitly classifies this stack's stage as production or not.

The classification drives everything that treats production differently: error-tracking
incidents (every production error group enters the incident queue), the stricter
delete-production permission, deploy gates, AI remediation autonomy limits, and the severity
of security findings (a database reachable from the internet is `HIGH` in production and `LOW`
elsewhere; production-only findings such as missing deletion protection are listed by
`stacktape validate` but not reported for other stages).

When omitted, the type chosen when the stage was created in the Stacktape Console decides.
Without either, Stacktape infers it from the stage name: `prod`, `production`, `prd`, and `live`
(case-insensitive, including segmented variants like `prod-eu` or `client-a-prod` and numbered
ones like `prod2`) count as production, while names carrying a rehearsal marker (`pre-prod`,
`prod-test`, `staging-live`) do not. Set it explicitly when your naming does not follow those
conventions.

This is a per-stage classification: with a TypeScript config, branch on the `stage` argument
to return different values for different stages.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  stageType: production
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tags`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<CloudformationTag>`

Tags applied to every AWS resource in this stack.

Useful for cost tracking, access control, and organization. Stacktape automatically
adds `projectName`, `stage`, and `stackName` tags — your custom tags are merged on top.

Max 45 tags.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tags:
    - name: team
      value: payments
    - name: costCenter
      value: '4100'
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions`

Stack-wide distributed tracing default.

Applies to every resource in the stack that supports tracing. Individual resources can override
it with their own `tracing` property (`false` opts a resource out). Enabling tracing requires no
code changes for Lambda-based resources — Stacktape attaches the OpenTelemetry instrumentation
automatically.

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
```

docs.title: StackConfig API Reference
StackConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `vpc`

- Required: no
- Type: `VpcSettings`

VPC configuration: the shared non-production network, or an existing VPC to reuse.

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
docs.content: # StackOutput API Reference

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `name`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Name of the output (used as the key in terminal and stack info file).

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `value`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Value to output. Typically a directive like `$ResourceParam('myApi', 'url')`.

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `description`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Human-readable description shown alongside the output.

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  outputs:
    - name: ApiUrl
      value: $ResourceParam('api', 'url')
      description: Public HTTPS endpoint of the API service
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `export`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Make this output available to other CloudFormation stacks.

Exported outputs can be referenced from other stacks using `$CfStackOutput()`.

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  outputs:
    - name: SharedBucketName
      value: $ResourceParam('assets', 'name')
      export: true
resources:
  assets:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.title: StackOutput API Reference
StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content: # StpIamRoleStatement API Reference

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Resource`

- Required: yes
- Type: `Array<string>`

ARNs of the AWS resources this statement applies to. Use `"*"` for all resources.

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Resource:
            - '*'
          Action:
            - rekognition:DetectLabels
            - rekognition:DetectText
```

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Action`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

AWS actions to allow or deny (e.g., `s3:GetObject`, `sqs:SendMessage`).

docs.title: StpIamRoleStatement API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `Condition`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Conditions under which this statement applies (e.g., IP restrictions, tag-based access).

**Example (YAML):**

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - s3:GetObject
          Resource:
            - 'arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'
          Condition:
            Bool:
              'aws:SecureTransport': 'true'
```

**Example (TypeScript):**

```ts
import { WebService, defineConfig, JsBundleImagePackaging } from 'stacktape';

export default defineConfig(() => {
  const api = new WebService({
    packaging: new JsBundleImagePackaging({ entryfilePath: 'src/server.ts' }),
    resources: { cpu: 0.25, memory: 512 },
    iamRoleStatements: [
      {
        Effect: 'Allow',
        Action: ['s3:GetObject'],
        Resource: ['arn:aws:s3:::my-secure-bucket/*'],
        Condition: { Bool: { 'aws:SecureTransport': 'true' } }
      }
    ]
  });

  return { resources: { api } };
});
```

docs.content: # VpcSettings API Reference

docs.title: VpcSettings API Reference
VpcSettings API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `reuseVpc`

- Required: no
- Type: `VpcReuseConfig`

Share a VPC with another Stacktape stack or use an existing VPC.

Useful when this stack needs to access VPC-protected resources (databases, Redis)
from another stack. By default, a production stage gets a VPC of its own and a non-production stage joins the
shared non-production network (see `shared`).

**Important:** Set this when first creating the stack. Adding it to an already
deployed stack can cause resources to be replaced and **data to be lost**.

docs.title: VpcSettings API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `shared`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`

Run this stage in the shared non-production network of its AWS account and region.

Non-production stages share one VPC (`stacktape-network`) and, when they need outbound internet, one small NAT
instance (`stacktape-network-nat`, ~$7.70/month for all of them). A new stage gets a VPC that takes no time to create,
and teams stay under the AWS limit of 5 VPCs per region. Each stage keeps its own security groups: resources in
`accessibilityMode: vpc` and internal load balancers admit only the stage's own workloads.

By default, a stage joins the shared network when it is non-production: `stackConfig.stageType`, then the type
chosen in the Stacktape Console, then the stage name decides (`dev`, `staging`, `test`, `preview`, `pr-12`,
`feature-x`, ...). Production stages and names that say neither (`main`, `acme`, `pre-prod`) get a VPC of their own. Set this
to `true` or `false` to choose yourself. Every deploy prints where the stage runs and why.

The choice is fixed by the first deploy that creates networked resources: moving a deployed stage to or from
the shared network means deleting and redeploying it. Stages with `reuseVpc`, MongoDB Atlas clusters, Kafka
clusters with function triggers, or `stackConfig.nat` set to `gateway` or `ha-ec2` always get a VPC of their own.

docs.title: HostingBucket API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: HostingBucket API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

    type: hosting-bucket
```

HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `fileOptions`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<DirectoryUploadFilter>`

Set HTTP headers (e.g., `Cache-Control`) for files matching specific patterns.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: 'assets/**'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `hostingContentType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "astro-static-website" | "gatsby-static-website" | "nuxt-static-website" | "single-page-app" | "static-website" | "sveltekit-static-website"`
- Default: `static-website`

Optimizes caching and routing for your type of frontend app.

**`single-page-app`**: For React, Vue, Angular, or any SPA built with Vite/Webpack.
Enables client-side routing (e.g., `/about` serves `index.html`). HTML is never browser-cached;
hashed assets (`.js`, `.css`) are cached forever.

**`static-website`** (default): For multi-page static sites. All files are CDN-cached
but never browser-cached, so users always see the latest content after a deploy.

**`astro-static-website`** / **`sveltekit-static-website`** / **`nuxt-static-website`**:
Framework-specific presets that cache hashed build assets (`_astro/`, `_app/`, `_nuxt/`)
indefinitely while keeping HTML fresh.

**`gatsby-static-website`**: Gatsby-specific caching following their recommendations.

You can override any preset's behavior using `fileOptions`.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `indexDocument`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`
- Default: `/index.html`

Page served for requests to `/`.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:

```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `injectEnvironment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Inject deploy-time values into HTML files as `window.STP_INJECTED_ENV.VARIABLE_NAME`.

Useful for making API URLs, User Pool IDs, and other dynamic values
available to your frontend JavaScript without rebuilding.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiGateway:
    type: http-api-gateway
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      injectEnvironment:
        - name: API_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('apiGateway', 'url')
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `routeRewrites`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<CdnRouteRewrite>`

Route specific URL patterns to different origins (e.g., `/api/*` → a Lambda function).

Evaluated in order; first match wins. Unmatched requests go to the bucket.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiGateway:
    type: http-api-gateway
  frontend:
    type: hosting-bucket
    properties:
      uploadDirectoryPath: ./dist
      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      routeRewrites:
        - path: /api/*
          routeTo:
            type: http-api-gateway
            properties:
              httpApiGatewayName: apiGateway
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `useFirewall`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Name of a `web-app-firewall` resource to protect this site. Must have `scope: cdn`.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:

```yaml
    properties:

    properties:

      hostingContentType: single-page-app
      build:
        command: npm run build
      useFirewall: siteFirewall
```

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `writeDotenvFilesTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Write deploy-time values to a `.env` file in the specified directory.

Merges with existing `.env` content if the file already exists.

docs.title: HostingBucketProps API Reference
docs.content:

```yaml
resources:
```

# HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference

Resource type: `http-api-gateway`

HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `disabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Disable access logging.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiGateway:
    type: http-api-gateway
    properties:
      logging:
        disabled: true

    type: function
    properties:

        type: js-bundle

            method: '*'
```

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `format`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "CLF" | "CSV" | "JSON" | "XML"`
- Default: `JSON`

Log format. Logs include: requestId, IP, method, status, protocol, responseLength.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiGateway:
    type: http-api-gateway
    properties:
      logging:
        format: CLF
        retentionDays: 30
  apiHandler:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/index.ts
      memory: 512
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: apiGateway
            path: /{proxy+}
            method: '*'
```

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  archiveWorker:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/archive.ts
      logging:
        logClass: infrequent-access
```

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logForwarding`

- Required: no
- Type: `http-endpoint | highlight | datadog`

Forward logs to an external service (Datadog, Highlight.io, or any HTTP endpoint).

Uses Kinesis Data Firehose (~$0.03/GB). Failed deliveries go to a backup S3 bucket.

Choices:
- `http-endpoint` (`HttpEndpointLogForwarding`). Properties: `endpointUrl: string`, `gzipEncodingEnabled?: boolean`, `parameters?: unknown`, `retryDuration?: number`, `accessKey?: string`.
- `highlight` (`HighlightLogForwarding`). Properties: `projectId: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.
- `datadog` (`DatadogLogForwarding`). Properties: `apiKey: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiFunction:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/api.ts
      memory: 512
      timeout: 10
      logging:
        retentionDays: 90
        logForwarding:
          type: datadog
          properties:
            apiKey: $Secret('datadog', 'apiKey')
```

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:

- Required: no
- Type: `number: 1 | 120 | 14 | 150 | 180 | 1827 | 3 | 30 | 365 | 3653 | 400 | 5 | 545 | 60 | 7 | 731 | 90`
- Default: `30`

How many days to keep logs.

docs.title: HttpApiAccessLogsConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiGateway:
    type: http-api-gateway
    properties:
      logging:
        format: JSON
        retentionDays: 365
  apiHandler:

    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: ./src/index.ts
      memory: 512
      events:
        - type: http-api-gateway
          properties:
            httpApiGatewayName: apiGateway
            path: /{proxy+}
            method: '*'
```
