# KinesisStreamProps API Reference

Resource type: `kinesis-stream`

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `capacityMode`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "ON_DEMAND" | "PROVISIONED"`
- Default: `ON_DEMAND`

How the stream scales.

**`ON_DEMAND`**: Auto-scales, pay per GB. Recommended for most use cases.
**`PROVISIONED`**: You choose a fixed number of shards (1 MB/s write, 2 MB/s read each). More predictable costs.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# capacityMode
resources:
  eventStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      retentionPeriodHours: 48
  streamProcessor:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/process-records.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: eventStream
            batchSize: 100
            startingPosition: LATEST
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `enableEnhancedFanOut`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Deprecated: has no effect. Set `autoCreateConsumer: true` on a function's trigger instead.

This property never changed the deployed stream and is ignored; Stacktape prints a deprecation warning when it is
set. To give a function its own enhanced fan-out consumer with dedicated 2 MB/s read throughput per shard, set
`autoCreateConsumer: true` (or `consumerArn`) on its `kinesis-stream` trigger, as in the examples below.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# enableEnhancedFanOut
resources:
  fanoutStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      enableEnhancedFanOut: true
  realtimeConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/realtime.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: fanoutStream
            autoCreateConsumer: true
            startingPosition: LATEST
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `encryption`

- Required: no
- Type: `KinesisStreamEncryption`

Encrypt data at rest using a KMS key.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# encryption
resources:
  secureStream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      encryption:
        enabled: true
  secureConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/consume.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: secureStream
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `retentionPeriodHours`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `24`

How long records stay in the stream (hours). Range: 24–8,760 (365 days). Beyond 24h costs extra.

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# retentionPeriodHours
resources:
  auditTrail:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: ON_DEMAND
      retentionPeriodHours: 168
  auditConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/audit.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: auditTrail
            startingPosition: TRIM_HORIZON
```

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `shardCount`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `1`

Number of shards. Only used when `capacityMode` is `PROVISIONED`.

Each shard: 1 MB/s write (1,000 records/s), 2 MB/s read (shared across consumers).

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml

docs.title: KinesisStreamProps API Reference
docs.content:
# shardCount
resources:
  clickstream:
    type: kinesis-stream
    properties:
      capacityMode: PROVISIONED
      shardCount: 4
      retentionPeriodHours: 72
  analyticsConsumer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/analytics.ts
      events:
        - type: kinesis-stream
          properties:
            kinesisStreamName: clickstream
            batchSize: 500
```

LogForwardingBase API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

```yaml
        logClass: infrequent-access
```

docs.title: LogForwardingBase API Reference
LogForwardingBase API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `logForwarding`

- Required: no
- Type: `http-endpoint | highlight | datadog`

Forward logs to an external service (Datadog, Highlight.io, or any HTTP endpoint).

Uses Kinesis Data Firehose (~$0.03/GB). Failed deliveries go to a backup S3 bucket.

Choices:
- `http-endpoint` (`HttpEndpointLogForwarding`). Properties: `endpointUrl: string`, `gzipEncodingEnabled?: boolean`, `parameters?: unknown`, `retryDuration?: number`, `accessKey?: string`.
- `highlight` (`HighlightLogForwarding`). Properties: `projectId: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.
- `datadog` (`DatadogLogForwarding`). Properties: `apiKey: string`, `endpointUrl?: string`.

```yaml
resources:

      memory: 512
      timeout: 10
      logging:
        retentionDays: 90

          properties:
            apiKey: $Secret('datadog', 'apiKey')
```

# MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference

Resource type: `mongo-db-atlas-cluster`

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "internet" | "scoping-workloads-in-vpc" | "vpc" | "whitelisted-ips-only"`
- Default: `internet`

Network access mode.

**`internet`**: Accessible from anywhere (credentials still required).
**`vpc`**: Only from resources in your VPC + any `whitelistedIps`.
**`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`**: Like `vpc`, but also requires security-group access via `connectTo`.
**`whitelisted-ips-only`**: Only from IP addresses listed in `whitelistedIps`.

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
providerConfig:
  mongoDbAtlas:
    organizationId: 5f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e
    publicKey: abcdefgh
    privateKey: $Secret('mongo-atlas-private-key')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
resources:
  appDb:
    type: mongo-db-atlas-cluster
    properties:
      clusterTier: M10
      version: '7.0'
      enableBackups: true
  api:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/index.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - appDb
```

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `whitelistedIps`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

IP addresses or CIDR ranges allowed to access the cluster (e.g., your office IP).

No effect in `internet` mode. In `vpc`/`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`, adds access for IPs outside the VPC.
In `whitelisted-ips-only`, these are the only IPs that can connect.

docs.title: MongoDbAtlasAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
providerConfig:
  mongoDbAtlas:
    organizationId: 5f1a2b3c4d5e6f7a8b9c0d1e
    publicKey: abcdefgh
    privateKey: $Secret('mongo-atlas-private-key')
    accessibility:
      accessibilityMode: whitelisted-ips-only
      whitelistedIps:
        - 203.0.113.10
        - 198.51.100.0/24
resources:
  appDb:
    type: mongo-db-atlas-cluster
    properties:
      clusterTier: M10
      version: '7.0'
      enableBackups: true
```

# ContainerDependency API Reference

Resource type: `multi-container-workload`

docs.title: ContainerDependency API Reference
ContainerDependency API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `condition`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "COMPLETE" | "HEALTHY" | "START" | "SUCCESS"`

The condition that the dependency container must meet.

Available conditions:

`START`: The dependency has started.
`COMPLETE`: The dependency has finished executing (regardless of success).
`SUCCESS`: The dependency has finished with an exit code of `0`.
`HEALTHY`: The dependency has passed its first health check.

docs.title: ContainerDependency API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: redis
          packaging:
            type: prebuilt-image
            properties:
              image: redis:7
          internalHealthCheck:
            healthCheckCommand:
              - CMD-SHELL
              - redis-cli ping || exit 1
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          dependsOn:
            - containerName: redis
              condition: HEALTHY
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

Run multiple containers together as a single unit with shared compute resources.

- Required: yes

docs.title: ContainerWorkload API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: ContainerWorkload API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

How to build or specify the container image.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: dockerfile
            properties:
              buildContextPath: ./api
              dockerfilePath: Dockerfile
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dependsOn`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ContainerDependency>`

Start this container only after the listed containers reach a specific state.

E.g., wait for a database sidecar to be `HEALTHY` before starting the app container.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: migrations
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/migrate.ts
          essential: false
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          dependsOn:
            - containerName: migrations
              condition: SUCCESS
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables injected at runtime. Use `$ResourceParam()` or `$Secret()` for dynamic values.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          environment:
            - name: NODE_ENV
              value: production
            - name: DATABASE_URL
              value: $ResourceParam('appDb', 'connectionString')
            - name: STRIPE_KEY
              value: $Secret('stripe', 'secretKey')
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - appDb
  appDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db', 'password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'

            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
```

ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`

If `true` (default), the entire workload restarts when this container fails.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `events`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<application-load-balancer | http-api-gateway | workload-internal | service-connect | network-load-balancer>`

How this container receives traffic (API Gateway, load balancer, or service-connect).

Choices:
- `application-load-balancer` (`ContainerWorkloadLoadBalancerIntegration`) — Triggers a container when a request matches the specified conditions on an Application Load Balancer.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `loadBalancerName: string`, `listenerPort?: number`, `priority: number`, `paths?: Array<string>`, `methods?: Array<string>`, `hosts?: Array<string>`, `headers?: Array<LbHeaderCondition>`, `queryParams?: Array<LbQueryParamCondition>`, `sourceIps?: Array<string>`.
- `http-api-gateway` (`ContainerWorkloadHttpApiIntegration`) — Triggers a container when an HTTP API Gateway receives a matching request.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `httpApiGatewayName: string`, `method: string: "*" | "DELETE" | "GET" | "HEAD" | "OPTIONS" | "PATCH" | "POST" | "PUT"`, `path: string`, `authorizer?: cognito | lambda | aws-iam`, `payloadFormat?: string: "1.0" | "2.0"`.
- `workload-internal` (`ContainerWorkloadInternalIntegration`) — Opens a container port for connections from other containers within the same workload.. Properties: `containerPort: number`.
- `service-connect` (`ContainerWorkloadServiceConnectIntegration`) — Opens a container port for connections from other compute resources in the same stack.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `alias?: string`, `protocol?: string: "grpc" | "http" | "http2"`.
- `network-load-balancer` (`ContainerWorkloadNetworkLoadBalancerIntegration`) — Triggers a container when a request is made to a Network Load Balancer.. Properties: `containerPort: number`, `loadBalancerName: string`, `listenerPort: number`.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: web
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/index.ts
          events:
            - type: application-load-balancer
              properties:
                loadBalancerName: appLb
                priority: 1
                paths:
                  - /*
                containerPort: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
  appLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
```

ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `secrets`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<SecretEnvironmentVar>`

Sensitive environment variables fetched by ECS instead of stored in the task definition.

Each `valueFrom` must be an exact `$SsmParam(...)` or `$Secret(...)` directive.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait after SIGTERM before SIGKILL (2-120).

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

docs.content:

```yaml
resources:

        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
```

docs.content:
## Property: `logClass`

- Required: no
- Type: `string: "infrequent-access" | "standard"`
- Default: `standard`

Choose the lower-ingestion-cost CloudWatch Logs class for logs that you inspect only occasionally.

`infrequent-access` still supports Logs Insights, but it does not support live tail, metric or subscription
filters, embedded metrics, or Stacktape log forwarding. A log group's class cannot be changed after it is
created, so use this for new resources or stages.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadContainerLogging API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

docs.content:
## Property: `strategy`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "AllAtOnce" | "Canary10Percent15Minutes" | "Canary10Percent5Minutes" | "Linear10PercentEvery1Minutes" | "Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes"`

How traffic shifts to the new version during deployment.

`Canary10Percent5Minutes`: 10% first, then all after 5 min.
`Canary10Percent15Minutes`: 10% first, then all after 15 min.
`Linear10PercentEvery1Minutes`: 10% more every minute.
`Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes`: 10% more every 3 minutes.
`AllAtOnce`: Instant switch.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadDeploymentConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: web
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/index.ts
          events:
            - type: application-load-balancer
              properties:
                loadBalancerName: appLb
                priority: 1
                containerPort: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      deployment:
        strategy: Linear10PercentEvery3Minutes

    type: application-load-balancer
  smokeTest:
    type: function
    properties:

        type: js-bundle
```

## Property: `resources`

- Required: yes

CPU, memory, and compute engine (Fargate or EC2).

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `releaseCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `ReleaseCommand | option-2`

Run a command once on each deploy, in the deployed image, before any workload gets the new code.

Use it for database migrations. Stacktape runs the command in a one-off ECS task with the same image, environment
variables, secrets, IAM role and network access as the chosen container. The deploy waits for the task, prints its
logs, and stops if the command fails, so the running version keeps serving.

The old code keeps running against the new schema until the rollout finishes, so migrations must stay compatible
with it. A retry runs the command again, so it must be idempotent. Neither a failed deploy nor `stacktape rollback`
reverses what the command changed.

Choices:
- `ReleaseCommand` (`ReleaseCommand`) — A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.. Properties: `command: string`, `runWhenChanged?: Array<string>`, `timeout?: number`, `container?: string`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `scaling`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadScaling`

Auto-scaling: how many instances and when to add/remove them.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: api
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      scaling:
        minInstances: 2
        maxInstances: 10
        scalingPolicy:
          keepAvgCpuUtilizationUnder: 70
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions | option-2`

Distributed tracing for this workload.

Overrides the stack-wide `stackConfig.tracing` setting: `false` opts this workload out, `true`
opts it in with the stack-wide sampling, an object opts it in with its own settings.

When enabled, Stacktape runs an OpenTelemetry collector as an additional container in the task
and points every container's OpenTelemetry SDK at it (`http://localhost:4318`) through standard
`OTEL_*` environment variables. The containers need the OpenTelemetry SDK in the application (any
language) — spans they emit are picked up without further configuration.

Traces are stored in your AWS account via X-Ray Transaction Search; see `stackConfig.tracing`
for the account-level effects.

Choices:
- `TracingOptions` (`TracingOptions`). Properties: `enabled?: boolean`, `samplingRate?: number`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  workers:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      tracing: true
      containers:
        - name: worker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
```

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Run the workload in the private subnets, without a public IP, with outbound traffic through the stack's NAT.

What you get: the container has no public IP, and all of its outbound internet traffic leaves through the stack's
NAT with one static Elastic IP per availability zone (useful when a third party allowlists your IPs).

Requires `stackConfig.nat` (`ec2`, `ha-ec2` or `gateway`); the cost depends on that choice, and `gateway` adds a
per-GB processing fee on top. Workloads that only talk to AWS services and other stack resources do not need it.

docs.title: ContainerWorkloadProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: worker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/worker.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

Resource type: `multi-container-workload`

docs.title: LoadBalancerHealthCheck API Reference
LoadBalancerHealthCheck API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `healthCheckPort`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Health check port. Defaults to the traffic port.

docs.title: LoadBalancerHealthCheck API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  app:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      containers:
        - name: web
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/index.ts
          events:
            - type: application-load-balancer
              properties:
                loadBalancerName: appLb
                priority: 1
                containerPort: 3000
          loadBalancerHealthCheck:
            healthcheckPath: /health
            healthCheckPort: 3000
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
  appLb:
    type: application-load-balancer
```

LoadBalancerHealthCheck API Reference
docs.content:

# NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference

TCP/TLS load balancer for non-HTTP traffic (MQTT, game servers, custom protocols).

Resource type: `network-load-balancer`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `properties`

- Required: yes
- Type: `NetworkLoadBalancerProps`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `overrides`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Escape hatch to modify the underlying CloudFormation resources Stacktape creates.

Each key is the logical ID of one of the resource's CloudFormation child resources, as it appears in the template
(`stacktape synth` writes it). Each path inside it is relative to that child resource's `Properties`: write
`StorageEncrypted`, not `Properties.StorageEncrypted`. Use dot-notation for nested properties.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancer API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t3.micro
    overrides:
      MainDbDbInstance:
        StorageEncrypted: true
```

# NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference

Resource type: `network-load-balancer`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `port`

- Required: yes
- Type: `number`

Port this listener accepts traffic on.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  tcpLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      listeners:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 7777

  gameServer:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      containers:
        - name: game-server
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          environment:
            - name: PORT
              value: 7777
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 7777
                loadBalancerName: tcpLb
                listenerPort: 7777
```

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `protocol`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "TCP" | "TLS"`

`TCP` (raw) or `TLS` (encrypted). TLS requires a certificate (auto-created with `customDomains` or via `customCertificateArns`).

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  tlsLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      customDomains:
        - domainName: mqtt.mydomain.com
      listeners:
        - protocol: TLS
          port: 8883

  mqttBroker:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      containers:
        - name: broker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/broker.ts
          environment:
            - name: PORT
              value: 8883
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 8883
                loadBalancerName: tlsLb
                listenerPort: 8883
```

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `customCertificateArns`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

ARNs of your own ACM certificates. Not needed if using `customDomains` or TCP protocol.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  byoCertLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      listeners:
        - protocol: TLS
          port: 8883
          customCertificateArns:
            - arn:aws:acm:eu-west-1:123456789012:certificate/2b8f1c3e-4a5d-6e7f-8a9b-0c1d2e3f4a5b

  mqttBroker:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      containers:
        - name: broker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/broker.ts
          environment:
            - name: PORT
              value: 8883
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 8883
                loadBalancerName: byoCertLb
                listenerPort: 8883
```

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `whitelistIps`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Restrict access to specific IP addresses/CIDRs. Default: all IPs allowed.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerListener API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  restrictedLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      listeners:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 5432
          whitelistIps:
            - 203.0.113.0/24
            - 198.51.100.42/32

  tcpProxy:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      containers:
        - name: proxy
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/proxy.ts
          environment:
            - name: PORT
              value: 5432
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 5432
                loadBalancerName: restrictedLb
                listenerPort: 5432
```

# NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference

Resource type: `network-load-balancer`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `listeners`

- Required: yes
- Type: `Array<NetworkLoadBalancerListener>`

Listeners define which ports and protocols (TCP/TLS) this load balancer accepts traffic on.

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  multiPortLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      listeners:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 9000
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 9001

  gameServer:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      containers:
        - name: game-server
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/server.ts
          environment:
            - name: GAME_PORT
              value: 9000
            - name: ADMIN_PORT
              value: 9001
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 9000
                loadBalancerName: multiPortLb
                listenerPort: 9000
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 9001
                loadBalancerName: multiPortLb
                listenerPort: 9001
```

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `customDomains`

- Required: no
- Type: `option-1 | option-2`

Custom domains.

By default, Stacktape creates DNS records and TLS certificates for each domain.
If you manage DNS yourself, set `disableDnsRecordCreation` and provide `customCertificateArn`.

Backward compatible format `string[]` is still supported.

Choices:
- `option-1`
- `option-2`

docs.title: NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  secureLb:
    type: network-load-balancer
    properties:
      customDomains:
        - domainName: mqtt.mydomain.com
        - domainName: legacy.mydomain.com
          disableDnsRecordCreation: true
      listeners:
        - protocol: TLS
          port: 8883

  mqttBroker:
    type: multi-container-workload
    properties:
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      containers:
        - name: broker
          packaging:
            type: js-bundle
            properties:
              entryfilePath: src/broker.ts
          environment:
            - name: PORT
              value: 8883
          events:
            - type: network-load-balancer
              properties:
                containerPort: 8883
                loadBalancerName: secureLb
                listenerPort: 8883
```

NetworkLoadBalancerProps API Reference

# NextjsWebProps API Reference

Resource type: `nextjs-web`

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `appDirectory`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Directory containing your `next.config.js`. For monorepos, point to the Next.js workspace.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./apps/storefront
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `buildCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Override the default `next build` command.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      buildCommand: pnpm run build
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `cdn`

- Required: no
- Type: `SsrWebCdnConfig`

CDN cache controls for SSR routes and specific path patterns.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      cdn:
        disableInvalidationAfterDeploy: false
        defaultCachingOptions:
          minTTL: 0
          defaultTTL: 60
          maxTTL: 3600
        pathCachingOverrides:
          - path: /_server-islands/*
            cachingOptions:
              defaultTTL: 300
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `customDomains`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<DomainConfiguration>`

Attach custom domains with auto-managed DNS records and TLS certificates.

**Prerequisite:** A Route 53 hosted zone for your domain must exist in your AWS account.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      customDomains:
        - domainName: app.example.com
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dev`

- Required: no
- Type: `unknown`

Dev server config for `stacktape dev`. Defaults to `next dev`.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables for the SSR function. Use `$ResourceParam()` or `$Secret()` for dynamic values.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  database:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db', 'password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
          version: '16'
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      connectTo:
        - database
      environment:
        - name: NODE_ENV
          value: production
        - name: DATABASE_URL
          value: $ResourceParam('database', 'connectionString')
        - name: STRIPE_SECRET_KEY
          value: $Secret('stripe', 'secretKey')
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `fileOptions`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<DirectoryUploadFilter>`

Set custom headers (e.g., `Cache-Control`) for static files matching a pattern.

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  web:
    type: nextjs-web
    properties:
      appDirectory: ./
      fileOptions:
        - includePattern: '**/*.{js,css,woff2}'
          headers:
            - key: Cache-Control
              value: 'public, max-age=31536000, immutable'
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `iamRoleStatements`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<StpIamRoleStatement>`

Raw IAM policy statements for permissions not covered by `connectTo`.

Added as a separate policy alongside auto-generated permissions. Use this for
accessing AWS services directly (e.g., Rekognition, Textract, Bedrock).

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  processor:
    type: batch-job
    properties:
      container:
        packaging:
          type: js-bundle
          properties:
            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
      iamRoleStatements:
        - Effect: Allow
          Action:
            - textract:AnalyzeDocument
          Resource:
            - '*'
```

docs.title: NextjsWebProps API Reference
NextjsWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `releaseCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `ReleaseCommand | option-2`

Run a command once on each deploy, inside the VPC, before any workload gets the new code.

Use it for database migrations. The site's server functions hold only bundled code, so Stacktape builds an image of
the whole project and runs the command in a one-off ECS task, with this resource's environment variables and its
access to the resources in `connectTo`. The command runs from the project root. The deploy waits for the task,
prints its logs, and stops if the command fails, so the running version keeps serving.

Set `runWhenChanged` to your migration folder. Without it, each change of the project builds the image and runs the
command. Building the image needs Docker on the machine that deploys.

The old code keeps running against the new schema until the deploy finishes, so migrations must stay compatible
with it. A retry runs the command again, so it must be idempotent. Neither a failed deploy nor `stacktape rollback`
reverses what the command changed.

Choices:
- `ReleaseCommand` (`ReleaseCommand`) — A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.. Properties: `command: string`, `runWhenChanged?: Array<string>`, `timeout?: number`, `container?: string`.
- `option-2`

## Property: `channelName`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Name of a notification channel configured in the Stacktape Console.

Channels are created once per organization in the Console (**Monitoring** → **Channels**) and hold the
delivery credentials (Slack tokens, webhook URLs, ...). Referencing a channel by name lets many alarms and
uptime checks share one destination without repeating credentials in the config.

The referenced channel must exist in your organization — the deployment fails with a clear error if it
doesn't. Delivery happens through the Stacktape Console, so events routed to a console channel always
appear in the alert history.

docs.title: ConsoleChannelIntegrationProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  apiHealth:
    type: uptime-check
    properties:
      url: https://api.example.com/health
      notificationChannels:
        - type: console-channel
          properties:
            channelName: engineering-slack
```

## Property: `cdn`

- Required: no

CDN cache controls for SSR routes and specific path patterns.

### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
    type: nuxt-web
```

NuxtWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: NuxtWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
    type: batch-job

            entryfilePath: src/job.ts
```

docs.content:
## Property: `releaseCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `ReleaseCommand | option-2`

Run a command once on each deploy, inside the VPC, before any workload gets the new code.

Use it for database migrations. The site's server functions hold only bundled code, so Stacktape builds an image of
the whole project and runs the command in a one-off ECS task, with this resource's environment variables and its
access to the resources in `connectTo`. The command runs from the project root. The deploy waits for the task,
prints its logs, and stops if the command fails, so the running version keeps serving.

Set `runWhenChanged` to your migration folder. Without it, each change of the project builds the image and runs the
command. Building the image needs Docker on the machine that deploys.

The old code keeps running against the new schema until the deploy finishes, so migrations must stay compatible
with it. A retry runs the command again, so it must be idempotent. Neither a failed deploy nor `stacktape rollback`
reverses what the command changed.

Choices:
- `ReleaseCommand` (`ReleaseCommand`) — A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.. Properties: `command: string`, `runWhenChanged?: Array<string>`, `timeout?: number`, `container?: string`.
- `option-2`

```yaml
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      serverLambda:
        memory: 2048
        timeout: 25
        joinDefaultVpc: true
        logging:
          retentionDays: 30
```

docs.title: NuxtWebProps API Reference
NuxtWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `useFirewall`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Name of a `web-app-firewall` resource to protect this app. Firewall `scope` must be `cdn`.

docs.title: NuxtWebProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  cdnFirewall:
    type: web-app-firewall
    properties:
      scope: cdn
      defaultAction: Allow
      rules:
        - type: managed-rule-group
          properties:
            name: AWSManagedRulesCommonRuleSet
            vendorName: AWS
            priority: 10
  web:
    type: nuxt-web
    properties:
      useFirewall: cdnFirewall
```

# OpenSearchAccessibility API Reference

Resource type: `open-search-domain`

docs.title: OpenSearchAccessibility API Reference
OpenSearchAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "internet" | "scoping-workloads-in-vpc" | "vpc"`
- Default: `internet`

How the domain can be reached.

**`internet`**: Accessible from anywhere (still requires IAM credentials).
**`vpc`**: Only accessible from resources inside your VPC (functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, containers, batch jobs).
**`scoping-workloads-in-vpc`**: Like `vpc`, but also requires security-group access via `connectTo`.

**Cannot be changed after creation** — switching between internet and VPC modes requires a new domain.

docs.title: OpenSearchAccessibility API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
      accessibility:
        accessibilityMode: scoping-workloads-in-vpc
  indexer:
    type: function
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/indexer.ts
      joinDefaultVpc: true
      connectTo:
        - searchEngine
```

# OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference

Resource type: `open-search-domain`

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `instanceCount`

- Required: yes
- Type: `number`

Number of data nodes. More nodes = more storage capacity and query throughput.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 4
      storage:
        size: 80
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `instanceType`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Instance type for data nodes (e.g., `t3.medium.search`, `r6g.large.search`).

Data nodes store data and handle queries. For production, pair with dedicated master nodes.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dedicatedMasterCount`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Number of dedicated master nodes. Must be odd (3, 5, or 7) for quorum.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3
      storage:
        size: 50
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `dedicatedMasterType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Instance type for dedicated master nodes (e.g., `m5.large.search`). Manages cluster state, not data.

Recommended for clusters with 3+ data nodes to prevent split-brain. Use an odd count (3, 5, or 7).

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3
      storage:
        size: 50
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `multiAzDisabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Disable Multi-AZ replication. Not recommended — reduces availability and data durability.

Multi-AZ is auto-enabled for clusters with 2+ nodes. It distributes nodes across availability zones
so the cluster survives an AZ outage.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: t3.medium.search
        instanceCount: 2
        multiAzDisabled: true
      storage:
        size: 20
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `standbyEnabled`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Enable Multi-AZ with a standby AZ for highest availability (99.99% SLA).

Distributes nodes across 3 AZs with one as standby. The standby takes over instantly during failures
without re-balancing. Requires: version 1.3+, 3 dedicated master + data nodes, GP3/SSD instances.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3
        standbyEnabled: true
      storage:
        size: 50
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `warmCount`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`

Number of warm (UltraWarm) nodes for lower-cost storage of older data.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3
        warmType: ultrawarm1.medium.search
        warmCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
```

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `warmType`

- Required: no
- Type: `string`

Instance type for warm (UltraWarm) nodes — cheaper storage for infrequently accessed data.

Data on warm nodes is still searchable but with higher query latency. Great for retaining old logs
or time-series data at lower cost.

docs.title: OpenSearchClusterConfig API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  searchEngine:
    type: open-search-domain
    properties:
      version: '2.17'
      clusterConfig:
        instanceType: r6g.large.search
        instanceCount: 3
        dedicatedMasterType: m5.large.search
        dedicatedMasterCount: 3
        warmType: ultrawarm1.medium.search
        warmCount: 2
      storage:
        size: 50
```

# PrivateServiceProps API Reference

Resource type: `private-service`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `packaging`

- Required: yes
- Type: `js-bundle | prebuilt-image | dockerfile | buildpack`

Configures the container image for the service.

Choices:
- `js-bundle` (`JsBundleCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a bundled JavaScript or TypeScript entry file.. Properties: `requiresGlibcBinaries?: boolean`, `customDockerBuildCommands?: Array<string>`, `runtime?: string: "bun" | "deno" | "node"`, `entryfilePath: string`, `includeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeFiles?: Array<string>`, `excludeDependencies?: Array<string>`, `tsConfigPath?: string`, `emitTsDecoratorMetadata?: boolean`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromBundle?: Array<string>`, `dependenciesToExcludeFromDeploymentPackage?: Array<string>`, `outputModuleFormat?: string: "cjs" | "esm"`, `nodeVersion?: number: 16 | 17 | 18 | 19 | 20 | 21 | 22 | 23 | 24`, `disableSourceMaps?: boolean`, `outputSourceMapsTo?: string`, `minify?: boolean`, `minifyIdentifiers?: boolean`, `bundleAwsSdk?: boolean`.
- `prebuilt-image` (`PrebuiltCwImagePackaging`) — Uses a pre-built container image.. Properties: `repositoryCredentialsSecretArn?: string`, `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `image: string`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `dockerfile` (`DockerfileCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from your own Dockerfile.. Properties: `entryPoint?: Array<string>`, `dockerfilePath?: string`, `buildContextPath: string`, `buildArgs?: Array<DockerBuildArg>`, `command?: Array<string>`.
- `buildpack` (`BuildpackCwImagePackaging`) — Builds a container image from a project directory without a Dockerfile.. Properties: `sourceDirectoryPath?: string`, `startCommand?: string`, `buildCommand?: string`, `installCommand?: string`, `packages?: unknown`, `aptPackages?: Array<string>`, `buildEnvironment?: Array<EnvironmentVar>`, `railpackConfig?: unknown`.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `resources`

- Required: yes
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadResourcesConfig`

CPU, memory, and compute engine for the container.

Two compute engines:

**Fargate** (default): Serverless — just specify `cpu` and `memory`.
**EC2**: Specify `instanceTypes` for more control and potentially lower cost.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 1
        memory: 2048
        architecture: arm64
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `connectTo`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<string>`

Give this resource access to other resources in your stack.

List the names of resources this workload needs to communicate with. Stacktape automatically:

**Grants IAM permissions** (e.g., S3 read/write, SQS send/receive)
**Opens network access** (security group rules for databases, Redis)
**Injects environment variables** with connection details: `STP_[RESOURCE_NAME]_[PARAM]`

Example: `connectTo: ["myDatabase", "myBucket"]` gives this workload full access to both
resources and injects `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`, `STP_MY_BUCKET_NAME`, etc.

 What each resource type provides:

**`Bucket`** — read/write/delete objects → `NAME`, `ARN`

**`DynamoDbTable`** — CRUD + scan/query → `NAME`, `ARN`, `STREAM_ARN`

**`RelationalDatabase`** — network access + connection details → `CONNECTION_STRING`, `HOST`, `PORT`.
Aurora also gets `READER_CONNECTION_STRING`, `READER_HOST`.

**`MongoDbAtlasCluster`** — temporary credential-less access → `CONNECTION_STRING`

**`Redis`** — network access → `HOST`, `READER_HOST`, `PORT`

**`Function`** — invoke permission → `ARN`

**`BatchJob`** — submit/list/terminate → `JOB_DEFINITION_ARN`, `STATE_MACHINE_ARN`

**`EventBus`** — publish events → `ARN`

**`UserAuthPool`** — full control → `ID`, `CLIENT_ID`, `ARN`

**`SqsQueue`** — send/receive/delete → `ARN`, `NAME`, `URL`

**`SnsTopic`** — publish/subscribe → `ARN`, `NAME`

**`UpstashRedis`** → `HOST`, `PORT`, `PASSWORD`, `REST_TOKEN`, `REST_URL`, `REDIS_URL`

**`PrivateService`** → `ADDRESS`

**`EmailSender`** — scoped SES sending permission → `IDENTITY`, `IDENTITY_ARN`, `REGION`, `CONFIGURATION_SET_NAME`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      connectTo:
        - mainDb
        - uploads
  mainDb:
    type: relational-database
    properties:
      credentials:
        masterUserPassword: $Secret('db-password')
      engine:
        type: postgres
        properties:
          version: '16'
          primaryInstance:
            instanceSize: db.t4g.micro
  uploads:
    type: bucket
    properties: {}
```

PrivateServiceProps API Reference

- Required: no

PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `environment`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<EnvironmentVar>`

Environment variables injected into the container at runtime.

Use for configuration like API keys, feature flags, or secrets.
Variables from `connectTo` (e.g., `STP_MY_DATABASE_CONNECTION_STRING`) are added automatically.

- Required: no

PrivateServiceProps API Reference

## Property: `internalHealthCheck`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerHealthCheck`

Health check that auto-replaces unhealthy containers.

If a container fails the health check, it's terminated and replaced automatically.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      internalHealthCheck:
        healthCheckCommand:
          - CMD-SHELL
          - curl -f http://localhost:3000/health || exit 1
        intervalSeconds: 30
        retries: 3
```

PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `loadBalancing`

- Required: no
- Type: `PrivateServiceLoadBalancing`
- Default: `service-connect`

How traffic reaches this service from other resources.

**`service-connect`** (default, ~$0.50/mo): Direct container-to-container. Cheapest option.
Only reachable from other container-based resources in the stack.
**`application-load-balancer`** (~$18/mo): HTTP load balancer. Reachable from any VPC resource.


PrivateServiceProps API Reference

Port this service listens on. Injected as the `PORT` env var.

- Required: no

Protocol for metrics collection. Set to enable protocol-specific metrics (e.g., HTTP 5xx tracking).

docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:

    type: private-service
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `releaseCommand`

- Required: no
- Type: `ReleaseCommand | option-2`

Run a command once on each deploy, in the deployed image, before any workload gets the new code.

Use it for database migrations. Stacktape runs the command in a one-off ECS task with the same image, environment
variables, secrets, IAM role and network access as this service. The deploy waits for the task, prints its logs, and
stops if the command fails, so the running version keeps serving.

The old code keeps running against the new schema until the rollout finishes, so migrations must stay compatible
with it. A retry runs the command again, so it must be idempotent. Neither a failed deploy nor `stacktape rollback`
reverses what the command changed.

Choices:
- `ReleaseCommand` (`ReleaseCommand`) — A command that runs once on each deploy, before any workload gets the new code.. Properties: `command: string`, `runWhenChanged?: Array<string>`, `timeout?: number`, `container?: string`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
releaseCommand: npx prisma migrate deploy
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 2 (typescript)

```typescript
releaseCommand: {
  command: 'npx prisma migrate deploy',
  runWhenChanged: ['prisma/migrations']
}
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `scaling`

- Required: no
- Type: `ContainerWorkloadScaling`

Auto-scaling: add/remove container instances based on demand.

Traffic is automatically distributed across all running containers.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      scaling:
        minInstances: 2
        maxInstances: 10
        scalingPolicy:
          keepAvgCpuUtilizationUnder: 70
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `sideContainers`

- Required: no
- Type: `Array<ServiceHelperContainer>`

Helper containers that run alongside the main container.

**`run-on-init`**: Runs to completion before the main container starts (e.g., database migrations).
**`always-running`**: Runs for the entire lifecycle (e.g., log forwarders, monitoring agents).
Can reach the main container via `localhost`.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `stopTimeout`

- Required: no
- Type: `number`
- Default: `30`

Seconds to wait for graceful shutdown before force-killing the container.

The container receives `SIGTERM` first, then `SIGKILL` after this timeout. Must be 2-120.

A full deploy waits until the old containers have stopped, so an app that ignores `SIGTERM` makes every deploy
up to this much slower. Exit once in-flight work is done. A hot-swap deploy lets old containers stop in the
background. Services with a gradual `deployment` (blue/green) default to 2 seconds.

docs.content:
## Property: `tracing`

- Required: no
- Type: `TracingOptions | option-2`

Distributed tracing for this service.

Overrides the stack-wide `stackConfig.tracing` setting: `false` opts this service out, `true`
opts it in with the stack-wide sampling, an object opts it in with its own settings.

When enabled, Stacktape runs an OpenTelemetry collector as a sidecar container and points the
service's OpenTelemetry SDK at it (`http://localhost:4318`) through standard `OTEL_*`
environment variables. The service needs the OpenTelemetry SDK in the application (any
language) — spans it emits are picked up without further configuration.

Traces are stored in your AWS account via X-Ray Transaction Search; see `stackConfig.tracing`
for the account-level effects.

Choices:
- `TracingOptions` (`TracingOptions`). Properties: `enabled?: boolean`, `samplingRate?: number`.
- `option-2`

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  tracing:
    enabled: true
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.5
        memory: 1024
      tracing:
        samplingRate: 0.5
```

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT`

- Required: no
- Type: `boolean`
- Default: `false`

Run the workload in the private subnets, without a public IP, with outbound traffic through the stack's NAT.

What you get: the container has no public IP, and all of its outbound internet traffic leaves through the stack's
NAT with one static Elastic IP per availability zone (useful when a third party allowlists your IPs).

Requires `stackConfig.nat` (`ec2`, `ha-ec2` or `gateway`); the cost depends on that choice, and `gateway` adds a
per-GB processing fee on top. Workloads that only talk to AWS services and other stack resources do not need it.

docs.title: PrivateServiceProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
stackConfig:
  nat: ha-ec2
resources:
  api:
    type: web-service
    properties:
      packaging:
        type: js-bundle
        properties:
          entryfilePath: src/server.ts
      resources:
        cpu: 0.25
        memory: 512
      usePrivateSubnetsWithNAT: true
```

## Property: `accessibilityMode`

- Required: yes

Who can connect to this cache.

**`vpc`** (default): Any resource in the same VPC (functions with `joinDefaultVpc: true`, containers, batch jobs).

## Property: `instanceSize`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "cache.m4.10xlarge" | "cache.m4.2xlarge" | "cache.m4.4xlarge" | "cache.m4.large" | "cache.m4.xlarge" | "cache.m5.12xlarge" | "cache.m5.24xlarge" | "cache.m5.2xlarge" | "cache.m5.4xlarge" | "cache.m5.large" | "cache.m5.xlarge" | "cache.m6g.12xlarge" | "cache.m6g.16xlarge" | "cache.m6g.2xlarge" | "cache.m6g.4xlarge" | "cache.m6g.8xlarge" | "cache.m6g.large" | "cache.m6g.xlarge" | "cache.m7g.12xlarge" | "cache.m7g.16xlarge" | "cache.m7g.2xlarge" | "cache.m7g.4xlarge" | "cache.m7g.8xlarge" | "cache.m7g.large" | "cache.m7g.xlarge" | "cache.r4.16xlarge" | "cache.r4.2xlarge" | "cache.r4.4xlarge" | "cache.r4.8xlarge" | "cache.r4.large" | "cache.r4.xlarge" | "cache.r5.12xlarge" | "cache.r5.24xlarge" | "cache.r5.2xlarge" | "cache.r5.4xlarge" | "cache.r5.large" | "cache.r5.xlarge" | "cache.r6g.12xlarge" | "cache.r6g.16xlarge" | "cache.r6g.2xlarge" | "cache.r6g.4xlarge" | "cache.r6g.8xlarge" | "cache.r6g.large" | "cache.r6g.xlarge" | "cache.r7g.12xlarge" | "cache.r7g.16xlarge" | "cache.r7g.2xlarge" | "cache.r7g.4xlarge" | "cache.r7g.8xlarge" | "cache.r7g.large" | "cache.r7g.xlarge" | "cache.t2.medium" | "cache.t2.micro" | "cache.t2.small" | "cache.t3.medium" | "cache.t3.micro" | "cache.t3.small" | "cache.t4g.medium" | "cache.t4g.micro" | "cache.t4g.small"`

The size of each node. Affects memory, performance, and cost.

**Quick guide** (Valkey prices, Redis OSS is about 25% more):

**`cache.t4g.micro`** (~$0.013/hr, 0.5 GB): Development, testing, low-traffic apps.
**`cache.t4g.small`** (~$0.026/hr, 1.37 GB): Small production apps, session stores.
**`cache.m7g.large`** (~$0.12/hr, 6.38 GB): Production workloads with moderate data.
**`cache.r7g.large`** (~$0.16/hr, 13.07 GB): Large datasets, memory-heavy caching.

**Families:** `t` = burstable (cheap, variable). `m` = general purpose. `r` = memory-optimized.
Suffix `g` = ARM/Graviton (better price-performance).

This size applies to every node (primary + replicas). You can change it later without data loss.

## Property: `defaultUserPassword`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string`

Password of the `default` user. 16-128 printable ASCII characters.

Clients connect as user `default` with this password; all traffic is encrypted in transit (TLS).
Allowed special characters: `!`, `&`, `#`, `$`, `^`, `<`, `>`, `-`. Use `$Secret()` instead of hardcoding:

docs.title: RedisProps API Reference
docs.content:
### Example 1 (yaml)

```yaml
resources:
```

docs.title: RedisProps API Reference
RedisProps API Reference
docs.content:
## Property: `engine`

- Required: yes
- Type: `valkey-serverless | valkey | redis`

Engine: which software runs the cache and how AWS runs it.

**`valkey-serverless`**: Scales automatically, highly available across Availability Zones, no sizing decisions.
Billed per GB stored (minimum 100 MB, about $6/month when idle) plus per request. Cheapest for small datasets;
above roughly 150 MB of data a small `valkey` node costs less. Always runs in cluster mode: commands that touch
several keys (`MGET`, transactions, Lua scripts) must use keys in the same hash slot, so queue libraries such as
BullMQ need a hash-tag prefix like `{bull}`. Keyspace notifications are not supported.
**`valkey`**: Fixed-size nodes, billed per hour. Works with every Redis client and command pattern.
**`redis`**: Redis OSS nodes (versions up to 7.1). Kept for caches deployed before Valkey support.
Switch an existing cache to `valkey` in place (about 20 minutes): writes pause for a few seconds during the
switch (longer without replicas), the data and endpoint stay, and the switch cannot be reversed.

Switching between `valkey-serverless` and a node-based engine replaces the cache: it gets a new endpoint and loses
its data. Stacktape refuses that change; delete the cache (or rename the resource) to recreate it.

Choices:
- `valkey-serverless` (`ValkeyServerlessEngine`) — Valkey Serverless: no instances to size, scales automatically, billed per GB stored and per request.. Properties: `version?: string: "7" | "8" | "9"`, `maxDataGb?: number`, `maxEcpuPerSecond?: number`.
- `valkey` (`ValkeyEngine`) — Node-based Valkey: fixed-size nodes billed per hour, compatible with every Redis client.. ## Property: `instanceSize`

- Required: yes
- Type: `string: "cache.m4.10xlarge" | "cache.m4.2xlarge" | "cache.m4.4xlarge" | "cache.m4.large" | "cache.m4.xlarge" | "cache.m5.12xlarge" | "cache.m5.24xlarge" | "cache.m5.2xlarge" | "cache.m5.4xlarge" | "cache.m5.large" | "cache.m5.xlarge" | "cache.m6g.12xlarge" | "cache.m6g.16xlarge" | "cache.m6g.2xlarge" | "cache.m6g.4xlarge" | "cache.m6g.8xlarge" | "cache.m6g.large" | "cache.m6g.xlarge" | "cache.m7g.12xlarge" | "cache.m7g.16xlarge" | "cache.m7g.2xlarge" | "cache.m7g.4xlarge" | "cache.m7g.8xlarge" | "cache.m7g.large" | "cache.m7g.xlarge" | "cache.r4.16xlarge" | "cache.r4.2xlarge" | "cache.r4.4xlarge" | "cache.r4.8xlarge" | "cache.r4.large" | "cache.r4.xlarge" | "cache.r5.12xlarge" | "cache.r5.24xlarge" | "cache.r5.2xlarge" | "cache.r5.4xlarge" | "cache.r5.large" | "cache.r5.xlarge" | "cache.r6g.12xlarge" | "cache.r6g.16xlarge" | "cache.r6g.2xlarge" | "cache.r6g.4xlarge" | "cache.r6g.8xlarge" | "cache.r6g.large" | "cache.r6g.xlarge" | "cache.r7g.12xlarge" | "cache.r7g.16xlarge" | "cache.r7g.2xlarge" | "cache.r7g.4xlarge" | "cache.r7g.8xlarge" | "cache.r7g.large" | "cache.r7g.xlarge" | "cache.t2.medium" | "cache.t2.micro" | "cache.t2.small" | "cache.t3.medium" | "cache.t3.micro" | "cache.t3.small" | "cache.t4g.medium" | "cache.t4g.micro" | "cache.t4g.small"`

The size of each node. Affects memory, performance, and cost.

**Quick guide** (Valkey prices, Redis OSS is about 25% more):

**`cache.t4g.micro`** (~$0.013/hr, 0.5 GB): Development, testing, low-traffic apps.
**`cache.t4g.small`** (~$0.026/hr, 1.37 GB): Small production apps, session stores.
**`cache.m7g.large`** (~$0.12/hr, 6.38 GB): Production workloads with moderate data.
**`cache.r7g.large`** (~$0.16/hr, 13.07 GB): Large datasets, memory-heavy caching.

**Families:** `t` = burstable (cheap, variable). `m` = general purpose. `r` = memory-optimized.
Suffix `g` = ARM/Graviton (better price-performance).

This size applies to every node (primary + replicas). You can change it later without data loss.

- Required: no

Requires `numReplicaNodes >= 1`. Replica count can't be changed after creation.
